sentences.text:
This application coming on for admission this day, the   the following:
 ORDER ORDER 1.This is first application under Section 439 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973, filed by the applicant for grant of bail during trial.

2. The applicant is facing trial in connection with Crime No.43/2023, registered at Police Station Mahila Thana, District Ujjain, for the offence punishable under sections 376, 376(2)(n), 294 and 506 of IPC, under Section 3(I)(w)(ii), 3(2)(v) of SC/ST Act and 5l/6 of POCSO Act.

The applicant is Israr @ Sukku vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61643941/
1 in custody since 27.04.2023.
3.As per the prosecution story

entities.text: Israr @ Sukku vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , the allegations against the applicant is that he outraged the modesty of the prosecutrix, hence, a case was registered against him.
4.Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.
He is in custody since 27.04.2023.
The prosecutrix has been examined before the trial Court.
Statement of the prosecutrix has been recorded in which her age has been recorded as 23 years.
She has not supported the prosecution story and turned hostile.
Conclusion of trial will take considerable long time.
Hence, the applicant may be enlarged on bail.
5. Learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer and prays for rejection of the bail application.

6. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and looking to the facts and circumstances of the case and the fact that the prosecutrix has turned hostile, I am of the view that it is a case in which applicant may be released on bail.
Consequently, first bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

7. It is directed that the applicant/accused be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court for securing his presence before the said Court on all the dates of hearing fixed in this regard during trial.

It is also directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) Cr.P.C.
8.

This order shall remain effective till the end of the trial but in case of bail jump and breach of any of the pre-conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective and cancelled without reference to this Bench.
Certified Copy as per rules.

(PREM NARAYAN SINGH) JUDGE VD Israr @ Sukku vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61643941/
